title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR — articular ἡ ἁμαρτία not always original sin
pass_a_gloss: GAR: Granted Paul often marks original sin inhering in human entrails by ἡ ἁμαρτία—still not every use must mean that sin. Anyone who has read Paul on sin (Rom 6:2, 6, 23; 2 Cor 15:56; 2 Thess 2:3; Heb 12:4) sees the range.
pass_b_english: GAR. Although the Apostle more often designates original sin, inhering in the entrails of humans, by the name he hamartia, it is nevertheless not necessary that wherever he uses that word, that sin be understood: which anyone will easily recognize who has read Paul speaking of sin, Rom. VI. 2. 6. 23: 2. Cor. 15. 56: 2. Thess. 2. 3. Heb. XII. 4.
source_text: GAR. Etsi saepius peccatum originale, inhaerens in visceribus hominum, nomine ἡ ἁμαρτία designat Apostolus, non est tamen necessarium, ut ubicumque vocabulum illud usurpat, intelligatur id peccatum: quod facile agnoscet, qui Paulum legerit de peccato loquentem, Rom. VI. 2. 6. 23: 2. Cor. 15. 56: 2. Thess. 2. 3. Heb. XII. 4.

choices.choice: Articular hamartia often original—but not everywhere
